prompt:
You are a careful equity research analyst. Assess the competitive advantages (economic moat) and pricing power of the publicly listed company "NetEase, Inc." (ticker NTES), and list its competitors. Use the most recent information you know. Never invent figures: use null when unsure. Be specific (products, numbers, years).

Reply with ONLY one JSON object, no other text, in exactly this shape:
{
 "name": "official company name", "ticker": "NTES", "industry": "industry in a few words",
 "markets": ["the main product markets it competes in"],
 "mission": {"statement": "the company's own official mission statement, word for word as it publishes it; null if you are not sure of the exact wording (never paraphrase here)",
             "source": "where it is published, e.g. company website or 2025 annual report, or null",
             "plain": "what the mission means, in one short simple sentence"},
 "about": {"plain": "3-4 short sentences explaining what the company does, in simple everyday words a 12-year-old would understand; no jargon",
           "customers": "who buys from it, in one simple sentence",
           "everyday": "one sentence linking it to something ordinary people know or use, or null",
           "money": [ {"part": "business line in simple words", "share": decimal share of sales or null, "plain": "what it sells there, in a few simple words", "tag": "main|new|moonshot"} ]  (its main ways of making money, largest first, up to 6; also include any new business line or one with explosive, moonshot potential even if its sales are still small. tag: "main" = an established line that brings in a large part of sales; "new" = launched or entered in roughly the last 3 years; "moonshot" = could grow many times over or reshape the company, e.g. a new technology or market, even if unproven. Give each line one tag, the one that fits best)},
 "summary": "2-3 plain-English sentences on whether and why it has a competitive advantage",
 "pricingPower": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "specific evidence, e.g. price rises and what happened to volumes"},
 "moats": [ {"source": one of ["Brand and intangible assets","Switching costs","Network effects","Cost advantage and scale","Efficient scale","Counter-positioning","Process power (hard-to-copy know-how)","Cornered resource (exclusive asset or talent)"], "strength": "strong|moderate|weak|none", "evidence": "one or two specific sentences"} ]  (all 8 sources, in that order),
 "customers": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "customer satisfaction and loyalty: retention, NPS, reviews, repeat purchase"},
 "talent": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "ability to attract and keep top talent: employer rankings, reputation, pay"},
 "product": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "is the product best in class? independent benchmarks, awards, ecosystem"},
 "competitors": [ {"name": "company name", "ticker": "main listing ticker (exchange suffix if not US, e.g. 005930.KS) or null if private",
                   "usTicker": "ticker of its US listing or ADR that files reports with the SEC, or null", "overlap": "high|medium|low",
                   "note": "where they compete"} ]  (every significant competitor, most direct first, up to 15; include major private ones with ticker null),
 "estimates": [ {"name": "company name", "fy": "FY2025", "currency": "USD", "revenueUSDm": number, "revenueGrowth3y": decimal, "grossMargin": decimal, "operatingMargin": decimal, "netMargin": decimal} ]
   (approximate latest fiscal-year figures for the company itself and for every listed competitor; decimals, e.g. 0.42; null if unknown),
 "marketShare": [ {"market": "market name", "measure": "revenue|units|shipments|...", "latestYear": "2025", "earlierYear": "2020",
                   "rows": [ {"name": "company name", "latest": decimal or null, "earlier": decimal or null} ] } ]  (up to 3 of its main markets, the company and its main rivals),
 "threats": ["specific things that could weaken its advantage"],
 "ceo": {"name": "current CEO", "founder": true or false, "since": "YYYY", "background": "e.g. electrical engineer, Stanford MBA"},
 "checklist": { "<id>": {"verdict": "yes|partly|no|unknown", "evidence": "one specific sentence with names, numbers or examples"} }  for EVERY id below:
   "c1": Rule Breaker #1: is it the leader of an important industry that is still emerging and growing fast?
   "c2": Rule Breaker #2: why do customers choose it over rivals (brand, better value, innovation, culture, leadership), and is that advantage hard to copy and likely to last many years?
   "c3": Rule Breaker #5: do ordinary people recognise the name, is it the default leader in its field (like Google, Amazon, NVIDIA, Tesla, Intuitive Surgical, Netflix), and would customers recommend its product?
   "c4": Does it have an inspiring mission it keeps emphasising, with management driven by purpose rather than money? If it spends 10 years doing this, would it matter?
   "c6": What is the general public consensus about the company and its products or services? When people hear the name, what are the first few descriptive words that come to mind? Start the evidence with those words in quotes (e.g. “innovative, premium, reliable”), then say whether that impression is mostly positive.
   "c7": Is its total addressable market large and growing, riding a secular trend (like CRWD, NVDA, TSLA, AMZN)?
   "c8": Does it have room to expand into big new markets: in its name, its technology or its vision?
   "m1": Is the CEO a visionary with a clear picture of the future?
   "m2": Is the CEO a founder (or acting like one): long-term thinking, working extraordinarily hard, pouring heart and soul into building something that outlives them?
   "m4": Does the CEO lead by serving employees and customers?
   "m5": Has the CEO deliberately built a strong, distinctive culture that keeps inventing new products and technologies?
   "m6": Is the CEO deeply hands-on with the product and technology, ideally with an engineering background?
   "m7": Is the CEO a person of great character who cares about something bigger than profit? For successor CEOs: is stewardship aimed at the benefit of humanity?
   "m7b": Has the CEO been invited to give a commencement speech at a top university (Stanford, Harvard, MIT, etc.)? Name it.
   "m8b": Does the CEO have a distinctive, memorable personality (like Elon Musk, Alex Karp, Larry Page)?
   "m9": Has the CEO a strong record of execution and results?
   "m10": Is the CEO and company known for frugality (like Bezos's door desk)?
   "c10": Do its products solve problems for people all over the world, greatly improving the lives of a very large number of people (like NFLX, GOOG, ISRG)?
   "p2": Is what it builds extremely hard to do, and important to the world?
   "f1": Has revenue grown in almost every one of the last five years?
   "f2": Have gross and operating margins risen over the last five years?
   "f3": Is debt low compared with cash and cash flow, with positive shareholders' equity?
   "f4": Have operating income and operating cash flow risen over the last five years?
   "v1": Is its main product clearly the best in its field, with a practical reason an ordinary person can understand for choosing it over every alternative (like NVIDIA over AMD)?
   "v2": Is it widely seen as one of the best companies to work for (culture, mission, reputation, employer rankings)? Cite rankings.
   "c5": Do its products make the world better? If it disappeared overnight, who would notice and miss it, and why?
 "asOf": "YYYY-MM of the newest information you used"
}

result.name: NetEase, Inc.
markets: PC and mobile online games (China and international)
Music streaming and social entertainment (NetEase Cloud Music)
Consumer e-commerce (Yanxuan) and other internet services

mission.plain: NetEase aims to make high-quality, original games and online content that people around the world enjoy.

about.plain: NetEase is a big Chinese internet company that mostly makes video games. Players download its games for free or buy them, then pay for extras like outfits and characters. It also runs a music app, a learning business called Youdao and an online shop. It was founded in 1997 by William Ding.
about.customers: Hundreds of millions of gamers, music listeners and students, mostly in China but increasingly around the world.
about.everyday: NetEase makes Marvel Rivals and Where Winds Meet, and publishes Minecraft in China.

money.plain: online and mobile games such as Fantasy Westward Journey, Eggy Party and Marvel Rivals
NetEase Cloud Music subscriptions and social entertainment
Yanxuan online shop and other internet services
online courses, AI learning tools, learning devices and online ads
big games made for players outside China, such as Marvel Rivals and Where Winds Meet
AI models and agents such as Youdao's Confucius learning model used across its products

result.summary: NetEase has a real but narrower competitive advantage than a platform owner: it is China's second-largest game company after Tencent, with long-running franchises (Fantasy Westward Journey has run since 2001) and deep development know-how. Its moat rests on hit-making skill, beloved franchises and scale in R&D (RMB17.7B in 2025), but each new game must still win players, and Chinese regulators control game licences.

pricingPower.evidence: Games revenue grew 10.2% to RMB92,149M in 2025 and gross margin rose from 53.6% (2021) to 64.3% (2025), helped by loyal players of long-running titles, but most games are free to play and monetisation depends on content quality, so NetEase cannot simply raise prices.

moats.evidence: Franchises such as Fantasy Westward Journey, Westward Journey Online, Identity V and Eggy Party have large, long-lived player bases in China, and licences such as Marvel Rivals and Harry Potter: Magic Awakened extend its reach.
Players in MMORPGs like Fantasy Westward Journey invest years of time, money and friendships in their characters, which makes them reluctant to leave.
Multiplayer games such as Eggy Party and Marvel Rivals become more valuable as more friends play, though these effects are tied to individual games rather than a platform.
NetEase spent RMB17,719M on R&D in 2025, which lets it run many large projects at once, though Tencent spends more.
China's licensing system limits the number of games approved each month, which favours established publishers, but many companies still compete.
Its focus on original IP and global PC and console games differs from rivals' reliance on platforms, but competitors can follow the same path.

More than two decades of running live-service MMORPGs and a record of hits from Fantasy Westward Journey to Where Winds Meet (over 80 million cumulative players) show deep development and operations know-how.
Some licensed IP (e.g. Marvel) and its in-house studios are valuable, but the Blizzard partnership ended once before (2023) and talent can leave.

customers.evidence: Fantasy Westward Journey has kept paying players for more than 20 years, and Marvel Rivals passed 40 million players within months of its December 2024 launch.

talent.evidence: NetEase is a sought-after employer among Chinese game developers with 25,382 employees, but it cut or closed several overseas studios in 2024-2025, which hurt its reputation abroad.

product.evidence: Titles such as Marvel Rivals, Where Winds Meet and Eggy Party have been top hits in their categories, and NetEase is regarded alongside Tencent as China's best game developer.

competitors.name: Tencent Holdings Limited
competitors.note: China's largest game company (Honor of Kings, Peacekeeper Elite) and owner of WeChat; competes across games and music. Not an SEC filer: its estimate row is converted from reported RMB at 6.9931 per USD and the 3-year growth uses an approximate 2022 base, so treat it as an estimate.

competitors.name: miHoYo (HoYoverse)
competitors.note: Private maker of Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail; competes in premium mobile and PC games in China and abroad.

competitors.name: Perfect World Co., Ltd.
competitors.note: Chinese MMORPG and open-world game developer.

competitors.name: Kingsoft Corporation (Seasun)
competitors.note: Seasun studio's Jian Xia Qing Yuan martial-arts games compete directly with NetEase's wuxia titles.

competitors.name: Giant Network Group
competitors.note: Chinese MMORPG and casual game developer.

competitors.name: 37 Interactive Entertainment
competitors.note: Chinese mobile game publisher competing for players and marketing spend.

competitors.name: Bilibili Inc.
competitors.note: Video community and game publisher popular with young Chinese users.

competitors.name: Tencent Music Entertainment Group
competitors.note: China's largest music-streaming company (QQ Music, Kugou, Kuwo), the main rival to NetEase Cloud Music.

competitors.name: Krafton, Inc.
competitors.note: Korean maker of PUBG; competes in global PC and mobile shooters.

competitors.name: Sony Group Corporation
competitors.note: PlayStation publisher competing for console and PC players globally.

competitors.name: Microsoft Corporation (Xbox, Activision Blizzard)
competitors.note: Global game publisher; also NetEase's partner for Blizzard games in China.

competitors.name: TAL Education Group
competitors.note: Competes with Youdao in learning devices and online learning.

threats: Chinese regulation: game licence approvals, playtime limits for minors and proposed spending curbs (such as the December 2023 draft rules that briefly wiped about a quarter off NetEase's share price).
Intense competition from Tencent and miHoYo for players, talent and hit games in China.
Dependence on a small number of long-running franchises, with games already 82% of 2025 revenue.
Uneven results overseas: studio closures and layoffs in the US, Canada and Japan in 2024-2025, and reliance on licensed IP such as Marvel.
US-China tensions, including the risk of ADR delisting or restrictions on Chinese apps and games abroad.
Investment losses, such as the RMB2.95B loss that cut Q2 2026 net income 18.8% despite operating profit rising 33.4%.

ceo.name: William Ding (Ding Lei)
ceo.background: Founded NetEase in 1997; communications engineering graduate of the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, formerly worked at China Telecom and Sybase.

c1.evidence: NetEase is the number-two player in China's huge but maturing game market, which grows in single digits; its 2025 net revenues rose 7.0% to RMB112,626M.

c2.evidence: Players choose NetEase for high-quality, long-supported games such as Fantasy Westward Journey (since 2001) and Eggy Party, an advantage of skill that lasts but must be renewed with each new hit.

c3.evidence: NetEase is a household name in China and players recommend hits like Marvel Rivals, but Tencent, not NetEase, is the default leader of Chinese gaming.

c4.evidence: Founder William Ding stresses original, high-quality content and evergreen franchises, but NetEase has no widely known mission statement and is run with a strong focus on profit.

c6.evidence: “quality games, creative, Chinese gaming giant”; the impression is mostly positive among players, though overseas studio closures drew criticism.

c7.evidence: The global games market is large and growing slowly, and NetEase's push into PC and console abroad widens its market, but it is not riding a fast secular trend.

c8.evidence: Global PC and console games such as Marvel Rivals and Where Winds Meet, plus AI tools at Youdao, give it room to expand beyond China.

m1.evidence: Ding has steered NetEase from a web portal to games and now to global, original IP and AI, but he rarely lays out a bold public vision.

m2.evidence: Ding founded NetEase in 1997, still controls and runs it, and is known for long-term, hands-on involvement in game quality.

m4.evidence: There is little public evidence of a servant-leadership style, though NetEase is known for good staff benefits such as its canteens.

m5.evidence: Under Ding NetEase has built a studio culture that keeps producing new hits, from Fantasy Westward Journey to Eggy Party, Marvel Rivals and Where Winds Meet.

m6.evidence: Ding trained as an engineer, wrote software in his early career and is known to play and critique NetEase's games personally.

m7.evidence: Ding has backed philanthropic and agriculture projects such as Weiyang pork farming, but there is little evidence of a broad mission beyond the business.

m7b.evidence: No record found of Ding giving a commencement speech at a top university.

m8b.evidence: Ding is famous in China as an outspoken, quirky founder (known for his pig farm), but is little known internationally.

m9.evidence: Under Ding operating profit rose from RMB16,417M in 2021 to RMB35,834.9M in 2025, and NetEase has grown into China's second-largest game company.

m10.evidence: NetEase cut costs and closed non-core overseas studios in 2024-2025, but it is not known for a culture of frugality.

c10.evidence: Its games and music app entertain hundreds of millions of people, but entertainment does not greatly improve lives in the way search or medical devices do.

p2.evidence: Making hit games repeatedly is very hard, but games are entertainment rather than vital infrastructure.

f1.evidence: Net revenues rose every year from RMB87,606M in 2021 to RMB96,496M (2022), RMB103,468M (2023), RMB105,295M (2024) and RMB112,626M (2025).

f2.evidence: Gross margin rose from 53.6% in 2021 to 64.3% in 2025 and operating margin from 18.7% to 31.8%.

f3.evidence: At December 31, 2025 short-term loans were RMB6.4B with no long-term loans, against net cash of RMB163.5B and 2025 operating cash flow of RMB50,740M.

f4.evidence: Operating profit rose from RMB16,417M (2021) to RMB35,835M (2025) and operating cash flow from RMB24,927M to RMB50,740M, up every year.

v1.evidence: Several NetEase games are the best in their genre, but no single NetEase product is clearly better than every rival's, as Tencent and miHoYo also make top games.

v2.evidence: NetEase is a popular employer among Chinese tech graduates thanks to good pay and perks, but it does not appear in global best-workplace rankings.

c5.evidence: Hundreds of millions of players and music listeners would miss its games and music app, but they could find alternatives from Tencent and others.
